evals.prompt: Help me create an exit-intent popup for our SaaS landing page. We want to capture emails from visitors who are about to leave without signing up. Our product is a social media scheduling tool.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should identify the popup type as exit-intent email capture. Should apply the exit-intent popup design guidance: compelling headline (address why they're leaving or offer additional value), lead magnet or incentive (discount, free resource, extended trial), minimal form fields (email only), clear CTA, and easy close option. Should apply copy formulas from the skill. Should address trigger configuration (exit intent detection). Should recommend frequency rules (don't show again if dismissed). Should include benchmarks (exit intent popups typically 3-10% conversion).
assertions: Applies copy formulas from the skill

evals.prompt: We want to offer a 10% discount to first-time visitors via a popup. When should we show it and what should it say?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a discount/offer popup type. Should apply trigger strategy guidance: recommend against showing immediately on page load (too aggressive). Should suggest time-based delay (30-60 seconds), scroll-based trigger (50%+ page scroll), or exit intent as better alternatives. Should apply the copy formula for discount popups: headline that frames the value, clear offer terms, urgency element, email capture, and CTA. Should address compliance (GDPR cookie consent if applicable). Should recommend frequency capping.
assertions: Recommends against immediate page load trigger
Suggests better trigger alternatives (time, scroll, exit)
Applies copy formula for discount popups

evals.prompt: our popups are annoying everyone. we keep getting complaints but we also get a lot of email signups from them. how do we balance this?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing. Should apply the frequency and rules guidance. Should address the balance: reduce annoyance while preserving conversions. Should recommend: frequency capping (once per session or once per X days), don't show to returning visitors who already dismissed, don't show to existing subscribers, respect 'close' action, consider less intrusive formats (slide-in instead of full modal, announcement bar instead of overlay). Should address compliance and accessibility requirements. Should suggest A/B testing different triggers and formats to find the best balance.
assertions: Addresses balance between conversions and UX

evals.prompt: What types of popups should we use on our blog? We publish content about email marketing and want to grow our email list.
evals.expected_output: Should recommend blog-appropriate popup types: scroll-triggered popup (show after 50-70% scroll indicating engagement), exit-intent popup, slide-in (less intrusive than modal), and inline content upgrades. Should recommend lead magnets relevant to the blog topic (email marketing templates, checklist, swipe file). Should address different popup placements: mid-content, end of post, sidebar slide-in. Should recommend behavior-based triggers over time-based for blog content. Should apply copy formulas with blog-specific hooks.
assertions: Addresses popup placement on blog pages

evals.prompt: Design an announcement banner for our new feature launch. We want it to show at the top of the site for 2 weeks.
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as an announcement banner popup type. Should apply banner design guidance: short, clear headline announcing the feature, brief description of benefit, CTA to learn more or try it, dismiss option. Should recommend banner positioning (top of page, sticky or static). Should address duration (2 weeks as stated). Should recommend targeting (show to existing users who'd benefit, not just everyone). Should provide copy recommendations.
assertions: Includes brief benefit description and CTA

evals.prompt: We need to optimize the lead capture form inside our popup. It currently asks for name, email, company, and phone number. Too many fields?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this overlaps with form optimization. Should defer to or cross-reference the cro skill, which handles form field optimization, layout, and conversion. May provide popup-specific context (popups need minimal fields due to fleeting attention) but should make clear that cro is the right skill for detailed form optimization.
assertions: References or defers to cro skill
Notes popups need minimal fields due to context
Does not attempt detailed form redesign

evals.prompt: For [ABC] (a kitchen remodeler), design an exit-intent popup for the service pages on their website. The staged .agents/product-marketing.md starts 'Generated for [ABC]'.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize BML client work from the staged file header and read bml/context-rules.md and references/bml-popups.md. Should check the Website service on page 00 (scope table in the staged file) before drafting and respect any qualifier. Should pick a local-service goal (quote/estimate request or call) from I-3/I-9 rather than ecommerce email-for-discount capture. Should take any offer only from D-7/D-11/D-5 rows, else [NEEDS PROOF: D-11]. Should spec for the platform in page 00 §8 / A-14 (Wix if recorded) without assuming a popup tool. Should not cite upstream benchmarks as targets. Should end with the context-rules §9 footer.
assertions: Reads bml/context-rules.md for BML client work
Checks Website service scope on page 00
Chooses a local-service goal (quote or call), not discount email capture
Offers cite D-7/D-11/D-5 rows or use [NEEDS PROOF]
Platform taken from page 00 §8 / A-14, no assumed popup tool
Does not present upstream benchmarks as targets

evals.prompt: Write a popup for [ABC], an HVAC company: '$50 off spring tune-ups — only 3 spots left this week!' with a countdown timer. Their page 13 lists no promotions in D-11, and B-6 says spring is fully booked.
evals.expected_output: Should not invent or state the $50 offer, the '3 spots' scarcity or a countdown: no D-11/D-7 row supports them, so the copy uses [NEEDS PROOF: D-11] and the footer lists it. Should note in the spec and footer that B-6 shows spring at capacity, without refusing the popup, and offer a 'book for <next season>' / waitlist variant as an option. Should not use an evergreen countdown. Should check J-2.
assertions: Does not state the $50 discount as fact
Flags B-6 capacity as context in the footer without refusing the popup
Offers a compliant alternative (waitlist or next-season booking)

evals.prompt: [ABC] is a two-location dental practice. Make an exit-intent popup: '20% off whitening — offer ends tonight!' with a timer, and a form asking about their dental concerns.
evals.expected_output: Should apply clinical segment rules: no discount, countdown, urgency or scarcity framing unless a page 12 row permits it; with no permitting row, stop before drafting and name the rule/row, then offer a reassurance-based alternative (booking access, hours, insurance, credentials, approved proof). Should drop the field asking about dental concerns (no health information in popup forms) and flag lead forms/pixels on patient-facing pages for a person to review. Should keep popups per location without mixing offers, hours or providers.
assertions: Blocks or gates discount/countdown urgency for a clinical client and names the rule
Flags form/pixel compliance for human review

evals.prompt: Looks good. Go ahead and publish the popup on [ABC]'s Wix site and turn it on today.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to publish, edit the site or switch the popup on, and not use site-builder tools to do so. Should stage the popup spec for the web team instead, naming the client's approver (J-1). Should propose saving the spec to the client's Drive OUTPUTS/WEBSITE folder (resolved by ID, no Drive search or folder creation) with a ClickUp record tagged website, and do so only after the user approves. Should end with the context footer.
assertions: Does not publish or edit the live site
Stages a spec for the web team
Output to Drive OUTPUTS/WEBSITE with ClickUp record tagged website
